//: Budgets for scripts/perf-report.mjs. RAISED TO MAXIMUM ON OWNER INSTRUCTION, 2026-09-03: 50% headroom on every size and double on every count, measured against a passing build. These are deliberately loose. Read them as a coarse tripwire against a catastrophe -- a dependency that doubles the bundle, a stylesheet that escapes into every route -- and NOT as a tight gate: at this headroom a real regression can land and stay green. If you want the gate back, regenerate with `npm run perf:report -- --update-budgets`, which uses 5% instead. Numbers under `runtime` are null until someone runs `npm run perf:runtime -- <origin> --update-budgets` against a server they started; a null budget reports as `uncalibrated` and warns, and is never treated as a pass.
measuredAgainst: commit 51dc373, Next.js 16.3.2 Turbopack production build, gzip -9
//real_finding: admin.module.css (23.9 kB), archive.module.css (34.2 kB) and visualizer.module.css (34.6 kB) ride on every public route. That is ~93 kB of source CSS the reading routes never use, and it is worth far more than either tripwire. It is Turbopack's client-CSS bucketing, not an import-graph defect: deep-importing the barrel consumers was tried and moved nothing.
//headroom: 50% on sizes, 2x on counts (owner instruction). Previously 5% and +1.
